tools.name: machine_create
tools.description: Create one VM/CT directly when the user asks for a machine. Defaults: Debian 13 VM, 2 vCPU, 2 GiB RAM, 20 GiB disk. Supply an SSH public key inline or use saved keys. No discovery or preview call is required; admission checks run during creation. Waits up to 55 seconds and returns verified readiness and SSH details in operation.result; only call operation_get if still pending. dry_run=true is optional for preview requests. Use VMs for Docker, OVS, Mininet or databases. CTs do not support packages, runcmd, health_checks or nested_virt. Use deployment_apply for multiple machines, connections or publications.

network_access.description: tenant allows all same-tenant primary traffic. restricted permits SSH/publications and declared connections only; choose restricted for app/database isolation. Restricted machines cannot attach unfiltered experiment NICs.

health_checks.description: Optional checks after cloud-init. Examples: {"type":"http","port":80,"path":"/","status":200}, {"type":"tcp","port":5432}, {"type":"service","service":"nginx"}. HTTP/TCP always target 127.0.0.1; specify port, not a URL. No checks means application readiness is not verified.

tools.name: deployment_plan
tools.description: Preview machines, allowed service connections and public endpoints together. Use machine names; no host or physical topology needed. Set network_access=restricted on connection destinations to enforce isolation; tenant mode allows all tenant machines. Optional networks/attachments are advanced L2 experiments. Checks aggregate quota/capacity; missing SSH keys become requirements. No resource writes or reservations. This is the complete preview: apply the same specification once with deployment_apply when authorized; do not repeat a dry-run or create each resource separately. Publications can reference existing machine names with no machines array.

HTTP/TCP always target 127.0.0.1; specify port, not a URL. No checks means application readiness is not verified.

tools.name: deployment_apply
tools.description: Create a group of machines, connections and publications in one call when authorized. Use deployment_plan only when a preview is wanted, then apply the same specification. Reserves the entire group and waits up to 55 seconds for completion; result includes SSH and public endpoints. Only call operation_get if still pending. Default rollback removes only newly created resources; keep retains them for repair. Reuse idempotency_key after a lost response.

tools.name: operation_get
tools.description: Get a background operation, or list the latest 50 tenant operations. With id, waits up to 55 seconds for completion to reduce repeated calls; other queries stay responsive. Use wait_seconds=0 for an immediate status. Queued means not reserved. Inspect terminal result/error/cleanup and follow next_action (revise_request means invalid inputs must be corrected, not retried); poll no faster than poll_after_seconds.

tools.name: operation_retry
tools.description: Resume a failed operation using its original allocation and durable checkpoints. A rolled-back deployment gets a fresh attempt; cleanup_failed retries cleanup first. Does not repeat a succeeded operation.

instructions: WinLab machines; tools only, no MCP resources. Use whoami when asked about identity or all visible tenants' used/limit/remaining quotas, service.version and capabilities. These are authoritative; capability questions do not need deployment previews. Use catalog_get for images/sizes, capacity_get only when asked about shared physical capacity. For a request to create one machine, call machine_create directly with a public key; defaults are Debian 13 VM, 2 vCPU, 2 GiB RAM, 20 GiB disk. No discovery or preview is required. Use deployment_apply to describe machines, connections (from/to/port), and publications (machine/protocol/port/sub for HTTPS) together. Use network_access=restricted for destinations that should accept only declared service connections. The default tenant mode allows all same-tenant traffic; extra networks/NICs are advanced unfiltered L2 experiments. Creation waits up to 55 seconds for verified readiness and returns a durable operation. Inspect its state/result/error; only use operation_get if still pending. Queued jobs have not reserved capacity. Use a stable idempotency_key after a lost submission response. Waiting jobs resume automatically; follow next_action. Completion returns SSH entries and public endpoints. For a local client, merge the returned ssh_config into its SSH configuration when authorized, verify with ssh -G, then present ssh_short. Before setup, use the direct ssh command. The alias needs no DNS change and is scoped by tenant. Publication verification=routing_configured does not verify an application's external HTTP response. Follow next_action for failures: operation_retry preserves allocations; revise_request means fix invalid inputs before a new submission. Managed private networks assign IPs automatically. Machine readiness includes cloud-init completion and requested application checks; SSH alone is insufficient. Use VMs for Docker, Mininet and databases. memory_mb/swap_mb are MiB; disk_gb is GiB. Preview when the user asks to plan or compare before creating. Authorized creation can apply directly. Destructive operations still require their confirmation fields. deployment_plan is the complete preview; do not repeat it with deployment_apply(dry_run=true) or manually execute its resources one by one. Previews never reserve or write resources; audit is recorded. Trust quota_before/delta/quota_after and resource_changes=false; follow-up list/quota/key calls are unnecessary just to verify a preview. Missing SSH public keys do not block planning; they are required for actual creation and can be passed inline without saving. Previews do not test guest boot or commands. Tenant membership is verified on every request; eligible tenants register automatically after sign-in.
